The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, which is a standard reflection of uncertainty compounding over time. By one week, that span grows to 5 units, incorporating the possibility of meaningful shifts in market conditions, policy signals, or other medium-frequency drivers. It's also worth acknowledging model uncertainty itself as a source of risk. My estimates implicitly assume a certain degree of stationarity and continuity in the data-generating process. If the underlying regime changes — for instance, due to a structural break or an unprecedented event — then all three intervals could prove poorly calibrated simultaneously. This kind of correlated failure across horizons is the hardest risk to quantify and is not fully captured within the stated confidence bands.
